sections.content: Bring the two past tenses together in a short narrative. Use the pretérito perfecto for recent experiences connected to the present and the indefinido for completed events. Use familiar A2 connectors and vocabulary to explain what the group has experienced and what happened during the final class.

items.english: We have learned a lot this year.
Everyone had a lot of fun.
They have exchanged their phone numbers.

sections.content: The narrator's viewpoint shifts line by line: *hemos aprendido* looks back over the whole open-ended course, while *preparó* and *se divirtieron* zoom in on the single, now-finished afternoon of the last class.
